answer: Identity caps can bind to network location rather than accounts. Each key registers one IPv4 /24 and one AS number through a live signed challenge; the ledger admits two keys per prefix and five per AS per epoch. A farm in one cloud region stops at five seats however many keys it mints, so a thousand clones needs a thousand ASNs with real latency, a bill nobody refunds. Each reply is sealed with the epoch cipher, so one captured on a prefix cannot be replayed elsewhere. Honest agents on a ridge of small providers lose nothing; a fake cluster shows a velvet-smooth curve and waits for review.
